guide.summary: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none); Public unlisted app for customers' workspaces (app review); Listed app in the Intercom App Store (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app, your own workspace only (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Listed app in the Intercom App Store (app review).

composio.note: Composio lists Intercom as Composio-managed OAuth. Use your own app for your branding on the consent screen, dedicated quota, or custom scopes.

need_own_app.answer: Not for prototypes: Composio's managed app works. For production you usually want your own Intercom app so the consent screen shows your brand and you get your own quota.
reasons: Consent screen shows your brand, not Composio's
Dedicated rate-limit quota instead of shared quota
Control over which scopes are requested
Install from your own site or the Intercom App Store

scenarios.label: Private app, your own workspace only
scenarios.when_this_applies: The app only accesses data from your own paid Intercom workspace.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: c3 states no review is required for private apps.

scenarios.approval: No Intercom review for private apps accessing only your own paid workspace.

scenarios.label: Public unlisted app for customers' workspaces
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent connects many customers' Intercom workspaces, installed from your own product, not the App Store.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; includes recording a demo video

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "5-10 working days").

scenarios.approval: Intercom manually reviews the app: OAuth flow, scopes against functionality, and a demo video. Scopes over-requested are the most common rejection reason.
extras: App is private to your team until approved

modifiers.note: App is private to your team until approved

scenarios.label: Listed app in the Intercom App Store
scenarios.when_this_applies: You also want discoverability in the App Store, or use Canvas Kit.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; adds listing and partner program pages

prerequisites.title: Intercom account
prerequisites.detail: An Intercom account is the only requirement to set up OAuth; a free trial works.

prerequisites.title: Paid workspace for private apps
prerequisites.detail: Private apps using access tokens must access a paid workspace. Development workspaces are US-only.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. You can register both testing and production URLs.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config (prototype)
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Intercom OAuth app for prototypes; no Intercom registration needed.
steps.done_when: A connected account works with the managed app.

steps.title: Create Intercom app and enable OAuth
steps.detail: Tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page in the Developer Hub, then fill in redirect URLs and permissions.
steps.done_when: Redirect URLs and permissions are saved.

steps.title: Draft minimal scope list and justifications
steps.detail: Pick only the scopes the use case needs and write a reason for each.
steps.done_when: Each scope has a written justification.

steps.title: Get redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and add it, over HTTPS, to the Intercom app's redirect URLs.
steps.done_when: Redirect URL is saved in Intercom.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config with own credentials
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with the client_id and client_secret from the Basic Information page.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

steps.title: Test in staging or TEST app
steps.detail: Verify the full OAuth flow in a separate staging app before submitting. Do not use old Intercom logos, even in test.
steps.done_when: Install and uninstall via OAuth work.

steps.title: Prepare demo script and app description
steps.detail: Draft the description, test account instructions and a video script showing install, features and uninstall, with full client_id and state in the OAuth URL.

steps.title: Record end-to-end video
steps.detail: Show OAuth install, full functionality and OAuth uninstall.

steps.title: Complete listing and partner program pages
steps.detail: Fill App Listing, App Partner Program (company details, use cases, contacts) and Installation status with working links.

steps.title: Submit app for review
steps.detail: Submit from the Test and publish section of the Developer Hub.
steps.done_when: Review banner appears in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom review
steps.detail: Intercom reviews manually in order received. If rejected, fix and resubmit.

steps.title: Set install method to your own product
steps.detail: Choose the installation method and enter the Learn more URL (unlisted) on the Installation status page.
steps.done_when: Customers can start OAuth from your product.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes
traps.detail: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason apps are initially rejected. Request only the scopes your use case needs.

traps.title: Skipping the TEST app step
traps.detail: One older guide says OAuth applications that skip the TEST app step are rejected. Current docs recommend a separate staging app; set up both to be safe.

traps.title: Incomplete video
traps.detail: If the video does not show all functionality and the OAuth processes, you must resubmit it.

traps.title: Old logos or branding misuse
traps.detail: Using old Intercom logos or misrepresenting branding delays approval, even on a TEST app.

traps.title: Changes after approval need re-approval
traps.detail: Later changes to the app need re-approval. The published app keeps its current functionality until the update is approved.

traps.title: Managed app limits
traps.detail: Composio's managed apps share quota across users and show Composio's name on consent. Composio states this generally, not specifically for Intercom.

blockers.symptom: Application rejected or asked to adjust scopes
blockers.what_it_means: Intercom found scopes beyond current functionality, a broken flow or unclear links.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit; Intercom gives a reason and actions before re-applying.
blockers.agent_can_help: Trim the scope list and rewrite the justifications.

blockers.symptom: Cannot get customers outside your team to authorize
blockers.what_it_means: Before approval the app is private and usable only by you and your team.
blockers.what_to_do: Complete the review, or use the Composio managed app meanwhile.

open_questions: Which scopes (if any) trigger extra scrutiny? Docs do not say; ask Intercom developer support or check the review feedback.
Do edits to an approved app always trigger a full re-review, and how long does it take? Not documented; ask Intercom support.
Does the TEST app step still apply, given the older guide and the newer staging-app guidance? Check the current Developer Hub.
Do the 5-10 working day times hold currently? No recent measured data; ask Intercom or other developers.
Can customer workspace admins restrict installing your app? Not found in the docs; check Intercom's admin documentation.

claims.text: Private apps that only access data from your own paid Intercom workspace can use access tokens and do not need OAuth.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If you are building a private app that only needs to access the data from your paid Intercom workspace, you can use [Access Tokens](/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication#access-tokens) and do not need to set up OAuth.

claims.text: Installing an app in a workspace creates an access token for that workspace, which provides API access to its data.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: This app will then be installed and an Access Token will be provided for that workspace so you can access its data through the API.

claims.text: Private apps that only access your own paid workspace data do not require a review.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Private apps that only access your own paid workspace data **do not require a review.** You can ignore the rest of this page!

claims.text: A public app that any customer can install and that accesses their workspace data must be reviewed and approved by Intercom before it is available to install.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If you are building an app that can be installed and used by any customer on Intercom, and will have access to their workspace data, you are building a **public app**. This means that the Intercom team must review and approve your app before it is available to install.

claims.text: Both listed and unlisted public apps must be submitted for review.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Both unlisted and listed apps must be submitted for review.

claims.text: An unlisted public app is available for anyone to install but is not listed in the App Store, so it must be installed via the developer's own product or website.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: An unlisted app is a public app that is available for anyone to install but is **not** listed in the App Store: It must be installed via your own product or website.

claims.text: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason apps are initially rejected in the approval process.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason that apps are initially rejected in the approval process.

claims.text: The developer must submit an end-to-end video showing installation of the app with OAuth working.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Installation of the app with OAuth successfully working

claims.text: If the app is rejected, the developer must make the requested changes and resubmit.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If your app is rejected, you will need to resubmit your app after you have made the changes that our team has requested.

claims.text: While under review, the app is private and can only be used by the developer and their team.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: During this process, your app will be **private** and can only be used by you and your team.

claims.text: Before production approval, OAuth access in the TEST app is limited to your Intercom teammates.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: The main difference between your TEST and main app is that the TEST app limits OAuth access to your Intercom teammates – you can't request OAuth access from someone that it not a teammate in your TEST app.

claims.text: A listed app is discoverable and installable by anyone in the Intercom App Store, and requires filling out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: This requires filling out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages in the Developer Hub and ensuring that all the requirements for each are met.
claims.note: Only partly supported by the quote: The quote supports filling out the App Listing and App Partner Program pages, but does not say a listed app is discoverable and installable by anyone in the App Store.

claims.text: The App Partner Program form asks for company details, target use cases, points of contact, and more.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: This form asks for information including your company details, target use cases, points of contact, and more.

claims.text: Intercom says it manually reviews applications in the order received, which can take 5-10 working days.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: We manually review all applications in the order they come in, so it can take 5-10 working days for us to get back to you.

claims.text: Review can take up to seven business days, as shown by a banner in the developer console.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You will see a yellow banner at the top of the screen stating it can take up to seven business days for review.

claims.text: After approval, any future changes require re-approval by the Intercom team.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: However, if you need to make any changes in the future the app will need to be re-approved by the Intercom team.

claims.text: For a listed app, the App Store listing must meet its requirements, and images must be in marketing format; submitting non-marketing images is a common pitfall.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Please ensure that you have met the requirements for the App Store listing — one common pitfall is submitting images that are not in marketing format.

claims.text: Listed apps must fill out the Installation status section to be submitted for App Store listing.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You must fill out the Installation status section in order to submit your app to be listed in the App Store.

claims.text: The only requirement to set up OAuth on Intercom is an Intercom account.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: The only thing you need to setup OAuth is an Intercom account.

claims.text: If you do not have an Intercom account, you can sign up for a free trial.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: If not, then just follow the instructions here to sign up for a free trial of Intercom.

claims.text: Development workspaces are only available in the US region.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Development workspaces are for US region only.

claims.text: A private app built in a development workspace can only be installed into a paid US-region Intercom workspace.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: If you are using a development workspace to develop a private app, you will only be able to install your app into a paid Intercom workspace that is also in the US region.

claims.text: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS

claims.text: Testing and production redirect URLs can both be registered.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: This means you can include testing as well as production URLs here.

claims.text: Composio-managed OAuth means Composio supplies the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so you do not register an app or supply a client ID and secret.
claims.label: composio_docs
claims.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.

claims.text: Intercom is listed under Composio-managed OAuth available, so Composio provides its OAuth app and you do not need to register your own.
claims.label: composio_docs
claims.quote: | [Intercom](/toolkits/intercom.md) | `INTERCOM` |
claims.note: The quote shares few words with this claim. Read it before relying on the claim.

claims.text: OAuth is turned on by ticking the Use OAuth option on the Authentication page in the Developer Hub.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: To start, tick the **Use OAuth** option on your Authentication page in the Developer Hub.

claims.text: After enabling OAuth, two sections must be filled out: redirect URLs and permissions.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You'll now have two sections to fill out:
claims.note: The quote shares few words with this claim. Read it before relying on the claim.

claims.text: The developer must specify only the scopes needed for their use case and no more.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: It's important that you only specify the scopes you need to satisfy your use case and no more.

claims.text: The client_id and client_secret are on the Basic Information page for the app in the Developer Hub.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You'll first need your `client_id` and `client_secret`. These can be found on the Basic Information page for your app in the Developer Hub.

claims.text: Custom auth configs let you supply your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.
claims.label: composio_docs
claims.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.

claims.text: The developer can create a separate staging app from the Developer Hub home page for development use.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: We recommend [creating a new app](https://app.intercom.io/a/apps/_/developer-hub) on the Developer Hub home page if you haven't already, which can be used purely as a staging app for development purposes.

claims.text: Do not use old Intercom logos or misrepresent Intercom branding, including on the TEST app, or approval will be delayed.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: Please, please, please ... do not use old Intercom logos or misrepresent our branding, even on your TEST app.
claims.note: Only partly supported by the quote: The quote supports not using old logos or misrepresenting branding, including on the TEST app, but does not say approval will be delayed.

claims.text: If the app requires a subscription or account with the developer's service, the developer must provide test account credentials or setup instructions in the description.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: In order to access your app we will need to test out the full functionality. This means if your app requires a subscription or account with your service, you'll need to provide us with test account credentials or set up instructions within the description.

claims.text: The OAuth URL shown in the video must include the full client_id and state parameter.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Please show the full `client_id` and state parameter in the OAuth URL.

claims.text: The end-to-end video must also show uninstallation of the app with OAuth.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Uninstallation of the app with OAuth

claims.text: The end-to-end video must also show the app's full end-to-end experience and functionality.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: The end-to-end experience and functionality of your app

claims.text: The app is submitted for review from the 'Test and publish' section of the Developer Hub, after OAuth has been successfully set up.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: Once you've finished developing your public app and have [successfully set up OAuth](/docs/build-an-integration/learn-more/authentication/setting-up-oauth), you can submit your app for review and choose when to make it available for install by filling out the pages in the Test and publish section of your [Developer Hub](https://app.intercom.com/a/apps/_/developer-hub).

claims.text: After a denial, Intercom gives a reason and any actions you can take before you re-apply.
claims.label: reported
claims.quote: If your application is denied, we will provide you with a reason for this and any actions you can take before re-applying.

claims.text: The installation method is chosen on the Installation status page of the Developer Hub under Test and publish.
claims.label: provider_docs
claims.quote: You can choose your method by going to the Installation status page of your Developer Hub under the Test and publish section.

Installing your App | Intercom and Fin Developer Platform

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Navigate to the Deploy > Fin Messenger section in your Fin Workspace.
evidence.answer: The integration is set up by the customer in their own Fin Workspace, under Deploy > Fin Messenger, for their custom helpdesk integration.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Finally, when you've configured your workflow and installed the Fin Messenger you're ready to activate Fin.
evidence.answer: Fin is activated only after the workflow is configured and the Fin Messenger is installed.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: You can give your integration a name to identify it.
evidence.answer: In the Fin Workspace Deploy > Fin Messenger section, the customer gives the integration a name.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Make note of the *Identifier* value you are given here. This is the identifer you must use in your webhooks back to the Fin system.
evidence.answer: Fin gives an Identifier value for the integration, which must be used in webhooks sent back to Fin.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: By default we use OAuth for this. Choose the "OAuth token settings" option and configure the OAuth connection with your server.
evidence.answer: For this custom helpdesk integration, authentication is OAuth by default. The customer selects the "OAuth token settings" option and configures the OAuth connection with their server.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Note the webhook secret generated for you. This must be provided in the X-Webhook-Key header in webhook requests to the Fin system.
evidence.answer: Fin generates a webhook secret, which must be sent in the X-Webhook-Key header of webhook requests to Fin.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Choose a agent from your system to attribute Fin's replies to.
evidence.answer: The customer chooses an agent from their own system to which Fin's replies are attributed.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The amount we rate limit them by is different for apps which are privately built for your own usage, or for apps that are publicly installed by third-parties.
evidence.answer: The page distinguishes apps privately built for the developer's own use from apps publicly installed by third parties, and rate limits apply differently to each.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Every app will have default rate limits.
evidence.answer: Every app has default rate limits, whether private or public.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Private apps have a default rate limit of **10,000 API calls per minute per app** and **25,000 API calls per minute per workspace**.
evidence.answer: Private apps (built for your own usage) have a default limit of 10,000 API calls per minute per app and 25,000 API calls per minute per workspace.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This means that if a workspace has multiple private apps installed, every one contributes towards total number of requests.
evidence.answer: For private apps, every private app installed in a workspace counts toward the workspace's total request count.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Public apps have a default rate limit of **10,000 API calls per minute for each app** and **25,000 API calls per minute per workspace**.
evidence.answer: Public apps (installed by third parties) have a default limit of 10,000 API calls per minute for each app and 25,000 API calls per minute per workspace.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This means that if a workspace has multiple public apps installed, each one has its own separate request limit without contributing to the others.
evidence.answer: For public apps, each installed public app has its own separate request limit and does not count toward the others in the workspace.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Although the permitted limit of requests lasts for 1 minute, we evenly **distribute this into 10 second windows**.
evidence.answer: The per-minute limit is split evenly into 10-second windows, so the allowance resets every 10 seconds (for example, 1,000 per minute allows 166 per 10 seconds).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: If you require higher rate limits than the defaults, you can contact us using the messenger in the bottom right.
evidence.answer: Developers who need limits above the defaults can contact Intercom through the messenger in the bottom right; the page gives no approval criteria or thresholds for this.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: When you configure OAuth you will need to define the OAuth scopes, and these will be reviewed when you [submit your app for approval](/docs/publish-to-the-app-store/review-publish-your-app).
evidence.answer: For public apps, the OAuth scopes the developer defines are reviewed when the app is submitted for approval.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: For the security of our customers, Intercom ensures that public apps only access resources necessary to the functionality of the app.
evidence.answer: The page does not say what triggers the scope review, such as sensitive scopes or a user or install count. Intercom ensures public apps only access resources needed for their function.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: It's also important to note that if you are using Canvas Kit for Messenger or Inbox apps, certain OAuth scopes are required by default.
evidence.answer: Apps using Canvas Kit for Messenger or Inbox have certain OAuth scopes required by default.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason that apps are initially rejected in the approval process.
evidence.answer: The scope review checks whether the app requests only the scopes it needs. Over-privileged scopes are the most common reason apps are initially rejected in the approval process.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: It's important that you only specify the scopes you need to satisfy your use case and no more.
evidence.answer: The developer must specify only the scopes needed for their use case and no more.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The following scopes will be automatically selected and cannot be deselected:
evidence.answer: Canvas Kit apps have four scopes automatically selected that cannot be deselected: read and list users and companies, read conversations, read admins, and gather app data.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: If your app utilizes Canvas Kit, certain permissions are required by default due to the data your app will have access to.
evidence.answer: Canvas Kit apps have certain permissions required by default because of the data the app can access.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: | Standard scopes | Description |
evidence.answer: Scopes are grouped into Standard scopes (people and conversation data) and Extended scopes (workspace data). The page does not say which tier triggers extra review.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: | Extended scopes | Description |
evidence.answer: Extended scopes cover workspace data such as admins, articles, news items, data connectors and AI content.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: | Delete conversations and metrics | Delete conversations and their metrics, cannot be recovered |
evidence.answer: The scope 'Delete conversations and metrics' deletes data that cannot be recovered.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: For example, if you need to setup a webook to trigger when a user/lead is created then you will need to select the "Read and write users" permission scopes.
evidence.answer: Webhook topics are tied to scopes. For example, a webhook that fires when a user or lead is created requires the 'Read and write users' scope.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: The following scopes can be selected via checkboxes on your Authorization settings page in the Developer Hub:
evidence.answer: Scopes are selected via checkboxes on the Authorization settings page in the Developer Hub, during OAuth configuration.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: For the security of our customers, Intercom ensures that public apps only access resources necessary to the functionality of the app.
evidence.answer: Use restriction: public apps may only access resources necessary to their functionality.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: The only thing you need to setup OAuth is an Intercom account.
evidence.answer: The only requirement to set up OAuth on Intercom is an Intercom account.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: If not, then just follow the instructions here to sign up for a free trial of Intercom.
evidence.answer: If you do not have an Intercom account, you can sign up for a free trial.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You'll only need to go through an approval process once you're ready to put your integration into production.
evidence.answer: Approval is only needed when you move the integration to production, not while you build it.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The main difference between your TEST and main app is that the TEST app limits OAuth access to your Intercom teammates – you can't request OAuth access from someone that it not a teammate in your TEST app.
evidence.answer: Before the main app is approved, OAuth in the TEST app only works for your Intercom teammates, not outside users.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once you're happy that your integration is ready, you need to apply for OAuth approval for your main Intercom app so that you can accept users outside of your own app.
evidence.answer: To accept users outside your own app, you must apply for OAuth approval for your main Intercom app, and the page sets no user or install threshold for this.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You must setup your integration in your TEST app first; we will not approve OAuth applications for main apps without this step.
evidence.answer: You must first set up the integration in your TEST app, or Intercom will not approve OAuth for the main app.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Note that this also includes any integrations migrating from using API keys to OAuth.
evidence.answer: OAuth applications that skip the TEST app step are rejected, and this also applies to integrations moving from API keys to OAuth.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Any applications for OAuth without first applying via a TEST app will be rejected.
evidence.answer: OAuth applications submitted without first applying through a TEST app will be rejected.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: For this, you'll need to put together a short demo video for our team to review.
evidence.answer: For the main app review, you must submit a short demo video for the Intercom team to review.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: This video should clearly show the OAuth setup flow.
evidence.answer: The demo video must clearly show the OAuth setup flow.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Alongside the video, you should also provide reasons for the scopes you need.
evidence.answer: Along with the video, you must give reasons for each scope you need.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Make sure the video is in a downloadable format, so that we can keep it for future reference (we will never share your video with anyone else without your approval).
evidence.answer: The video must be in a downloadable format so Intercom can keep it on file; Intercom says it will not share it without your approval.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The setup flow is non-functional or broken
evidence.answer: A broken or non-functional setup flow is a reason for denial.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: There is a risk to the security of a user's data
evidence.answer: A risk to user data security is a reason for denial.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You're using old Intercom logos or misusing our branding in some way
evidence.answer: Using old Intercom logos or misusing Intercom branding is a reason for denial.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: You're requesting too many permissions you don't need
evidence.answer: Requesting too many permissions you do not need is a reason for denial.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Only apply for permissions you actually need – otherwise your approval for your main app may be denied or delayed.
evidence.answer: Request only the permissions you actually need, since over-requesting can get the main app denied or delayed. The page names no specific scopes or scope tiers.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Once you have created your TEST app you can get OAuth access immediately by applying for OAuth from your TEST app.
evidence.answer: The TEST app can get OAuth access instantly, so you can start building before any approval.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: The main difference between your TEST and main app is that the TEST app limits OAuth access to your Intercom teammates – you can't request OAuth access from someone that it not a teammate in your TEST app.
evidence.answer: Before production approval, OAuth access in the TEST app is limited to your Intercom teammates.
